history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV lists the town as Tiruppur, but the exact-name match - 'Arulmigu Kadu Anumantharaya Swamy Temple' - is the Hanuman temple on Dharapuram Road in DHARAPURAM, ~55 km south of Tiruppur city (district Tiruppur is correct). Documented as the Dharapuram temple. AMBIGUITY FLAG: a second 'Anumandaraya Swamy Temple' is listed on Sivanmalai Road in Tiruppur district (11.0385, 77.5353), closer to Tiruppur town, but its name does not match the CSV's 'Kadu Anumantharaya'; if the CSV meant that shrine, this file would need to move. Also note: a seawatersports.com page describes a 'Kadu Anumantharaya' temple in Kadu village, Kanyakumari district on the Tamiraparani - that text reads as unreliable AI-generated content and is NOT this temple (flagged, not used). The Dharapuram temple is a large Hanuman temple about 2 km from the Dharapuram main bus stand. Its speciality, per devotees, is that Lord Anjaneya stands under open sky with a Sowganthika flower in his hands; one reviewer records the local belief that the statue grows by an inch or so over time. Sannidhis exist for Rama-Sita-Lakshmana and for Narasimhar. TripAdvisor rates it 4.8/5 from 4 reviews (2017-2019).

name: Kadu Anumantharaya Swamy Temple
town_description: Dharapuram is an old Kongu Nadu town in Tiruppur district, about 55 km south of Tiruppur city on the road toward Palani. A historic settlement with several ancient temples, it is best known in this dataset for the Kadu Anumantharaya Hanuman temple, about 2 km from its main bus stand.
